bibliographic.title: Transforming Financial And Insurance Ecosystems Through Intelligent Automation, Secure Digital Infrastructure, And Advanced Risk Management Strategies
bibliographic.authors: Lahari Pandiri; Srinivasarao Paleti; Pallav Kumar Kaulwar; Murali Malempati; Jeevani Singireddy
bibliographic.citation_apa: Pandiri, L., Paleti, S., Kaulwar, P. K., Malempati, M., & Singireddy, J. (2023). Transforming financial and insurance ecosystems through intelligent automation, secure digital infrastructure, and advanced risk management strategies. Educational Administration: Theory and Practice, 29(4), 4777-4793. https://doi.org/10.53555/kuey.v29i4.9669

methodology.method_family: ecosystem perspective; conceptual discussion of digital transformation, risk management, and regtech
methodology.technology_context: intelligent automation, chatbots, robotic process automation, machine learning, natural language conversational artificial intelligence, AI trust models, regtech, digital platforms, trust services, identity blocks

eligibility.exclusion_reason: The article is a broad conceptual overview of digital transformation, intelligent automation, and risk management in financial and insurance ecosystems. It mentions chatbots and natural language conversational artificial intelligence only peripherally and does not center on governance of LLM-based or conversational AI systems.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Although the paper references chatbots, conversational AI, accountability-related terms, and regulated financial/insurance contexts, the provided text shows no specific focus on large language models or on conversational governance mechanisms such as guardrails, observability, human oversight, contestation, or post-deployment monitoring of conversational systems. The work is better classified as sector-level digital transformation and risk strategy than as evidence on conversational governance in LLM systems.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Deterministic triage scored the article as a central candidate largely via keyword hits (governance, chatbots, compliance), but full-text review shows only incidental mentions of conversational AI and no LLM-specific or conversational-governance analysis.

appraisal.notes: Conceptual sector overview without described empirical design, sample, data collection, or systematic analysis in the provided text. Claims about transformation mechanisms and risk strategies are presented discursively rather than through a reported research method.

cerqual.explanation: For the review's focus on conversational governance in LLM-based systems, the article offers only peripheral and generic references to chatbots and conversational AI within a broader financial/insurance automation narrative. No substantive conversational-governance findings or LLM-specific mechanisms are evidenced in the supplied text.

coding.theme: Digital transformation and risk management in financial and insurance ecosystems
coding.subtheme: Intelligent automation and trust-enabled digital infrastructure
rq_alignment: limited alignment: generic AI trust and fairness mentions
no clear alignment: LLM conversational governance

synthesis.main_claim: Financial and insurance ecosystems can be improved through digital infrastructures, intelligent automation, secure processing, and advanced risk management, with AI-enabled tools contributing to business effectiveness, risk evaluation, and customer interaction.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a high-level ecosystem perspective linking digital platforms, trust services, identity blocks, intelligent automation, regtech, and insurance risk management in financial and insurance markets.
synthesis.use_in_review: Not recommended as central or supporting evidence for conversational governance in LLM systems; at most marginal contextual background on chatbots and AI trust models in regulated financial/insurance settings.
